metadata.title: qf-pgpe: a verified pure-Rust projected Gross-Pitaevskii engine for quantum-fluid experiments, with a Python extension (the quantum-fluids module of rusty-SUNDIALS)
metadata.description: Classical-field (projected Gross-Pitaevskii) simulations of two-dimensional Bose fluids are usually scripts whose correctness is checked, when at all, by a few conservation laws. We describe qf-pgpe, the quantum-fluids module of the rusty-SUNDIALS numerical library: a pure-Rust integrating-factor RK4 engine for the projected equation on a periodic grid, a vortex instrument (periodic theta-function imprint, sub-grid detection, tracking), the registered estimators of vortex friction and diffusion, a thermal-state toolkit, a vortex-phonon scattering instrument, and a Python extension (pyo3, numpy) with a drop-in stepper. Every module is a port of a Python original of an ongoing pre-registered research programme and carries a numeric cross-check against it: estimators agree to 2e-14 on real vortex tracks, a 31-run scattering matrix to 5e-11, measurements on a shared thermal field to 1e-14; the engine is checked against known answers and against rusty-SUNDIALS' own CVODE (global error falling as dt^4.00). The cross-checks found three defects, one of them in the Python programme: its primary estimator of the mutual friction is biased low by vortex diffusion (-8 to -22 %), a flaw the registered synthetic gate had not shown. On one thread of a 2013 laptop CPU the engine is 4.3, 4.2, 2.7, 2.5 times faster per step than the numpy engine at N = 64, 128, 256, 512 (3.2 to 1.5 times against the fastest Python engine tried, torch on CPU), and the drop-in extension makes an end-to-end thermal-state measurement 5.3 times faster with identical results. No claim is made about GPU codes or other published solvers, which were not measured; intra-run threading, tried, did not help on this machine.
metadata.notes: Software paper of the qf-pgpe crate (rusty-SUNDIALS main, commit 72cad84). Companion to the vortex-transport and friction-law papers of the SocrateAI-Scientific-QuantumFluids programme.
